title: Shaft and chamber system found under the Queen's Chamber in early excavations, later sealed
place_text: Queen's Chamber, Great Pyramid, Giza, Egypt

tellings.quote: So they excavated this. They found a pit in the Queen's Chamber that was filled with rubble and dirt.
So this has again been reported in the archaeological excavation that there there is something like this below the Queen's Chamber.
tellings.difference: Gives no date for the excavation and does not mention the pit later being sealed.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of a shaft or chamber system under the Queen's Chamber that was reported in archaeological excavation.

as_told.title: Shaft below the Queen's Chamber reported in excavation
as_told.place_text: Queen's Chamber, Great Pyramid, Giza, Egypt

plain: Early excavations of the Great Pyramid at Giza, sometime between 1800 and the early 1900s, are said to have found a pit in the Queen's Chamber "filled with rubble and dirt", with a system of shafts and chambers below it that was later sealed. The researcher Jeffrey Drum tells Michels this, citing the original excavation reports. In a second telling he says only that the excavation reports describe "something like this below the Queen's Chamber", with no date and nothing about sealing. If true, the pyramid would have hidden spaces beneath it that are no longer open to anyone.
